title: Match diligence depth to third-party risk
applicability: Onboarding and periodic review of vendors, agents, consultants, and intermediaries
trigger_logic: Escalate when risk-based diligence is absent, stale, or materially weaker than the third party's risk profile.
recommended_action: Pause automated approval; obtain or refresh diligence and document the rationale for the risk tier.
notes: Screening control; not a legal or fraud determination.

title: Document the business rationale for using the third party
applicability: Vendor or intermediary engagement and invoice approval
trigger_logic: Escalate when no documented business need connects the third party, its services, and the transaction.
recommended_action: Request business-owner attestation and supporting scope documents before payment.
notes: Part of a broader risk-based program.

title: Verify services and compensation are reasonable
applicability: Invoices and payments to third parties
trigger_logic: Escalate when the contract does not clearly describe the services, evidence of work is missing, or compensation appears inconsistent with the industry and geography.
recommended_action: Perform scope-to-invoice and market-rate review; route unexplained variances for human approval.
notes: Compensation reasonableness is contextual; do not use a universal threshold.

title: Continue monitoring after onboarding
trigger_logic: Escalate when a relationship lacks refreshed diligence, training, audits, certifications, or risk-based monitoring during its lifecycle.
recommended_action: Refresh controls based on risk and document completion or an approved exception.
notes: Cadence should be risk-based.

title: Prevent re-engagement of rejected or terminated third parties
trigger_logic: Escalate when a prospective vendor matches a previously rejected, suspended, or terminated entity or its related parties.
recommended_action: Block automated onboarding and require compliance review with entity-resolution evidence.
notes: Use privacy-preserving entity matching.

title: Assess sanctions risk across parties and transactions
applicability: Customers, suppliers, intermediaries, counterparties, products, services, and geographies
trigger_logic: Escalate when a covered relationship or transaction has not been assessed against its sanctions exposure.
recommended_action: Apply documented risk assessment and route high-risk cases to the sanctions team.
source_title: A Framework for OFAC Compliance Commitments
notes: Legal applicability and list status must be checked at decision time.

title: Risk-rate parties during onboarding
trigger_logic: Escalate when onboarding lacks a documented sanctions risk rating based on submitted information and appropriate independent research.
recommended_action: Complete risk rating and enhanced review when warranted before enabling transactions.
source_title: A Framework for OFAC Compliance Commitments
notes: Use current official sanctions lists and qualified reviewers.

title: Keep screening logic and identifiers current
trigger_logic: Escalate when screening lists, identifier coverage, transliteration, alternate spellings, or system calibration are stale or incomplete.
recommended_action: Update lists and matching logic; retest before clearing affected alerts.
source_title: A Framework for OFAC Compliance Commitments
source_section: Internal Controls; Root Causes of Compliance Breakdowns
notes: A model score must not replace required legal screening.

title: Identify, interdict, escalate, report, and preserve records
applicability: Potential sanctions matches and prohibited transactions
trigger_logic: Escalate when a potential match can proceed without a documented path to stop or reject the transaction, investigate, report when required, and retain evidence.
recommended_action: Hold the transaction and follow the organization's approved sanctions procedure.
source_title: A Framework for OFAC Compliance Commitments
notes: Human and legal review required.

title: Possible split purchase below approval threshold
applicability: Purchase requests, tenders, and purchase orders
trigger_logic: Flag two or more processes by the same buyer for the same or similar item category within a short period when values cluster just below a competitive or approval threshold.
recommended_action: Aggregate related processes for review and document whether separate procurement was justified.
notes: Threshold and time window are jurisdiction-specific configuration.

title: Single bid in a competitive procedure
trigger_logic: Flag a competitive process with only one tenderer or one valid bid.
recommended_action: Review market outreach, specifications, timelines, and conflicts before award.
notes: A single bid can be legitimate; treat as a review signal.

title: Abnormal bidder address or phone
trigger_logic: Flag missing, implausible, duplicated, or anomalous bidder contact details, especially when shared across nominally independent bidders.
recommended_action: Perform entity resolution and validate contact information against independent sources.
source_section: R042 Abnormal bidder address or phone
notes: Normalize addresses and phones before matching.

title: Bidder contact matches project official
applicability: Procurement contacts and employee or official directories
trigger_logic: Flag when a bidder's address, phone, email, or other contact attribute matches a project official or procurement employee.
recommended_action: Route to an independent conflict-of-interest review and preserve matching evidence.
source_section: R043 Bidder contact matches project official
notes: Protect employee and supplier personal data during matching.

title: Large award-to-contract value change
trigger_logic: Flag a material difference between the awarded value and final signed contract value beyond the configured tolerance.
recommended_action: Verify approvals, scope changes, arithmetic, and publication accuracy.
source_section: R059 Difference between award and final contract amount
notes: Tolerance must reflect local rules and currency normalization.

title: Payments exceed contract value
trigger_logic: Flag when cumulative paid amount exceeds the current approved contract value after valid amendments and currency normalization.
recommended_action: Place the excess payment in review; reconcile amendments, taxes, credits, and exchange-rate treatment.
source_section: R068 Total payments exceed contract amount
notes: Compute at contract level and account for valid credits and amendments.

title: Amendment increases contract price
trigger_logic: Flag amendments that increase contract price, especially repeated or large increases relative to the original value.
recommended_action: Review justification, approval authority, competition impact, and cumulative increase.
notes: An increase is a signal, not proof of misconduct.

title: Delivered goods or services do not fulfill specifications
applicability: Receipt, inspection, acceptance, and invoice approval
trigger_logic: Flag failed inspections, rejected milestones, or material mismatch between delivered items and contractual specifications.
recommended_action: Hold acceptance or payment as allowed by contract; obtain inspection evidence and corrective action.
source_section: R073 Delivered work goods or services do not fulfill specifications
notes: Often requires document and human review rather than transaction data alone.

title: Review abnormally low bids
trigger_logic: Flag a bid whose price appears materially too low to support compliant performance when compared with estimates, peers, scope, or market evidence.
recommended_action: Seek written clarification and detailed price analysis; reject only under the applicable procedure if capability cannot be demonstrated.
source_title: Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers seventh edition
notes: Do not automatically reject on price alone.

title: Evaluate lifecycle cost and quality alongside price
applicability: Sourcing and award decisions where operating or maintenance cost is material
trigger_logic: Escalate when award analysis relies only on purchase price despite material lifecycle cost, quality, risk, sustainability, or non-price requirements.
recommended_action: Apply the documented evaluation method and preserve factors, period, assumptions, and weighting.
source_title: Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers seventh edition
source_section: Value for Money; Life Cycle Costing and Rated Criteria
notes: Weights and discount rates are procurement-specific.

title: Ground price reasonableness in comparable evidence
applicability: US federal proposal analysis and analogous internal price review
trigger_logic: Escalate when price approval lacks comparison to competition, prior prices adjusted for differences, parametric estimates, market prices, independent estimates, or market research.
recommended_action: Select and document one or more suitable comparison techniques before approval.
notes: Applicability outside federal acquisition requires local policy mapping.

title: Detect materially unbalanced line-item pricing
applicability: Offers with multiple priced line items
trigger_logic: Flag line items priced materially above or below reasonable cost or price relationships even when the total offer appears acceptable.
recommended_action: Assess performance and payment risk and document whether the imbalance creates unacceptable risk.
notes: Requires contextual price analysis.

title: Generate daily fraud reports and near-real-time alerts
trigger_logic: Escalate when monitoring cannot produce daily reports, real-time or near-real-time alerts, or a rapid stop capability during major fraud attacks.
recommended_action: Route alerts to trained staff and measure investigation and mitigation timeliness.
source_title: Security Rules and Procedures Merchant Edition
notes: Exact obligations depend on participant role and region.

title: Detect merchant deposit and refund anomalies
trigger_logic: Flag sudden volume or ticket-size increases, deposit-frequency changes, unusual credits, refunds above purchase volume, refunds to unseen accounts, and chargeback growth.
recommended_action: Compare with the merchant's history and category; investigate and consider a temporary hold under approved procedures.
source_title: Security Rules and Procedures Merchant Edition
notes: Use a baseline of at least 90 days where the rulebook requires it; configure new-merchant expectations separately.

title: Review monthly activity and business-model inconsistency
applicability: Merchants, payment facilitators, and sponsored merchants
trigger_logic: Flag changes in monthly transaction count or amount, refunds, confirmed fraud, average ticket, chargebacks, or activity inconsistent with the stated business model.
recommended_action: Open a merchant review with trend evidence and business-context verification.
source_title: Security Rules and Procedures Merchant Edition
notes: Seasonality and merchant category must be considered.

title: Detect shared-identifier and out-of-pattern payment activity
trigger_logic: Flag out-of-pattern transaction counts tied to the same email, phone, delivery address, browser fingerprint, device, PAN/BIN range, or source; also flag merchant or identifier mismatches and abnormal hours or geography.
recommended_action: Apply velocity limits and risk-based authentication or blocking, then investigate linked entities.
source_title: Security Rules and Procedures Merchant Edition
notes: Tokenize payment credentials and personal data.

title: Disclose supplier relationships that can impair objectivity
applicability: Supplier personnel and customer-company employee relationships
trigger_logic: Escalate undisclosed family, financial, or other personal relationships that may affect procurement or payment decisions.
recommended_action: Obtain disclosure and independent conflict review before award or payment approval.
source_title: Apple Supplier Code of Conduct and Supplier Responsibility Standards
source_section: Business Integrity and Conflicts of Interest
notes: Example of a company-specific policy; ingest the organization's own supplier code for production.

title: Maintain material transaction traceability
trigger_logic: Escalate when required transactional records cannot trace materials from source through relevant supply-chain stages.
recommended_action: Request missing chain-of-custody and transactional evidence before acceptance.
source_title: Apple Supplier Code of Conduct and Supplier Responsibility Standards
notes: Adapt to the applicable company's traceability standard.

title: Retain accurate supplier compliance records
trigger_logic: Escalate when required records are missing, inaccurate, altered, or unavailable for authorized audit and verification.
recommended_action: Preserve records, investigate integrity issues, and remediate access or retention gaps.
source_title: Apple Supplier Code of Conduct and Supplier Responsibility Standards
notes: Production rules should reference the applicable contract and corporate retention schedule.
